title: Induction-probes-scratchpad
content:
Quick context: trying to understand how "induction" style generalization is implemented in transformers and what that implies for long-context caching / prefix dedup strategies on Redwood. This is a messy brain dump — goals: build small, interpretable probes; get actionable signals for streaming/cache heuristics; identify low-hanging evals we can run on hosted workloads.

High-level takeaways so far (skimmed papers + early toy runs):
- Induction behavior: model learns to continue sequences by retrieving repeating subsequences — appears as attention to previous token pairs across long distances.
- Mechanism hypotheses: (1) explicit pair-matching attention heads (induction heads); (2) positional alignment via relative pos encodings; (3) cached KV representations that enable cheap jump-back retrieval.
- For inference platform: induction-like patterns suggest benefit from prefix-merge dedup if prefix repeats exactly; but beware approximate repeats (small token-level drift) — naive dedup can degrade quality.

Papers to reconcile:
- Olsson et al. (2022?) "Induction Heads" (arXiv link above) — main model of pair-attention + gating.
- Papers on emergent in-context learning (ICL) — overlap in observed dynamics but not identical mechanisms.
- Circuit-level analyses from transformer-circuits (multiple blog posts) — useful motifs (copy circuits, comparator heads).

Open questions / experiments to run (small -> medium):
1) Toy dataset probe: generate synthetic sequences with repeating subsequences and short pattern variants (insertions, 1-token noise). Measure attention concentration and logit-deltas when KV cache contains exact vs approximate repeat.
   - Metric: delta in next-token prob mass for predicting repeat continuation (and disagreement when we zero-out suspected induction heads).
   - Implementation notes: can use a 6-12 layer GPT2-small style model trained quickly on synthetic data; or use distilled open checkpoints for initial signal.
2) Head-masking ablations: identify candidate heads (high attn to repeating tokens). Mask and measure loss/accuracy on repeat continuation tasks. Track whether masking kills behavior or just shifts it.
3) Prefix-dedup stress test: on real user prompts (anonymized, consented sample), instrument repeated phrases at varying offsets and similarity. Evaluate generation differences when serving with prefix merge vs naive full-KV.
   - Concern: dedup might be safe for exact repeats but harmful for paraphrases that change conditioning subtly.
4) KV-compression experiment: instead of storing every token KV, cluster similar KV vectors in a windowed LRU and use representative vectors. Hypothesis: induction signals rely on precise pattern matching, so aggressive averaging could blur match signals.

Early sketch of evaluation harness:
- Generator: simple program that emits sequences like: [A B C X A B C ?] with variations (A->synonymA1, token dropout).
- Checkpoint pool: GPT2-small, LLaMA-7B-small-ish (quantized sim), and a tiny transformer trained on toy data.
- Observables: attention heatmaps, KV similarity matrices (cosine), token prob shifts when toggling cache/heads, inference latency impact of KV operations.

Practical Redwood takeaways I'm aiming for: 
- Binary rule: exact-prefix-dedup allowed by default (low risk), approximate-dedup as opt-in with evaluation thresholds.
- Metric to expose in Console: "induction-sensitivity score" per model/route — fraction of prompts where cache dedup changed top-1 by >X and reduced perplexity on repeats.
- A/B test plan: roll dedup to 1% traffic on hosted API with careful monitoring of regression alerts tied to evaluation prompts.

Notes / TODOs (personal):
- [ ] Implement toy generator and run on small models (deadline: 2024-10-14).
- [ ] Add a lightweight explainability hook in inference runtime to dump top-5 attention targets for last N tokens for sampled requests (talk to infra).
- [ ] Post initial results to #eng-applied-ml and schedule 30-min sync with Samir + Hannah.

Random scribbles / heuristics:
- When detection of exact repeat occurs, we could short-circuit by mapping future token logits to cached continuation distribution (fast-path). But need to attach confidence calibration.
- For approximate matches, use a fuzzy-match threshold on KV cosine > 0.97? need to empirically pick.
- Instrument cost implication: cache hits yield token compute savings but add KV similarity compute; tradeoff point depends on sequence length and model occupancy.

References and links I want to re-read:
- Induction heads paper (arXiv)
- Transformer Circuits blog posts: copy/copy head 
- Our PR: github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/42 (notes on microbench harness)

Slack breadcrumbs: saved a thread with user prompt examples (channel link above). Pull sample (anonymized) for prefix stress tests.

Questions for next sync: 
- Samir: can infra accept extra lightweight tracing for sampled requests without violating PII rules?
- Hannah: what user segments are safe to include in early A/B (signup bots vs paid customers)?
- Me: what's our resource budget for short model fine-tune / toy training (~1-2 A100 days ok?).

End of dump. Keep it messy — will clean into a one-pager after initial experiments.
